-To choose your own email before first start, run the install line with `setup` in place of `dev` instead, then `cd run-spool && ~/.local/bin/rer dev`. Explicit setup asks for missing required answers in an interactive terminal. With non-TTY input, put JSON such as `{"OWNER_EMAIL":"[address omitted]"}` in `.rer/local/setup-answers.json`, an ignored private file with mode `0600`, then run `rer setup --answers .rer/local/setup-answers.json --non-interactive` from the Spool checkout. The answers path must be relative and contained inside that checkout; absolute paths, traversal and symlinks are refused. Piping an email alone is not a setup answer. Saved answers are reused. To replace the temporary dev owner's address later, stop dev first and supply `OWNER_EMAIL` through that file. Keep addresses and secrets out of shell arguments. See [installation](docs/getting-started.md) for the file procedure.
+On the setup page, enter what to call this installation, your name and your email. You can change the installation name in **Settings → General**, and your name and email in **Settings → Members**. Hosted email changes require a recent sign-in or email verification.

-`rer dev` opens signed in as the owner. Open the private `RER_OPEN` link printed on this computer; its `#rer-dev=` fragment carries this checkout's owner gate. Keep the link and gate private. Local development reads **Spool Dev**; `rer demo` reads **Spool Demo** and adds sample data in disposable state. Mail is silently suppressed in dev and demo; there is no local outbox viewer. To invite someone locally, open **Settings → Members**, create an invitation and copy its pending invitation link. The invitee opens their own single-use, expiring invitation directly in a separate browser on this computer and presses **Confirm**. They receive only their membership and project access. Never send them the owner’s RER_OPEN link: it signs in as the owner. After removal, their member session loses access; ask the owner for a new invitation to rejoin.

 With rer dev v2 (using the rer version pinned in [package.json](package.json)), an ingest key created in dev works directly from your app against local Spool, and a deploy key works from your local build, without the owner gate. Allow your browser app's exact origin in Capture. Dev agent keys still need the gate for evidence and inert proposals: privately extract the `rer-dev` fragment value as `SPOOL_DEV_KEY` for the local agent CLI, as shown in [the agent guide](docs/WITH-YOUR-AGENT.md#local-agent-access). Never give the gate to a browser app. Every dev-minted key is refused by deployed Spool; create fresh keys there. Private archives exclude all project grants.
 
-A fresh installation opens `/setup`. Replace a lost key in Settings. To restore existing evidence instead, choose **Restore a private archive** before creating a project. Register the app's release/build before sending its errors; the setup test registers the release/build shown on that screen.

Name your installation and create the first project, then follow the three steps: save your key, send a test error and give the connection code to your developer. Register the app's release/build before sending its errors; the setup test registers the release/build shown on that screen.

 Export before reset and import only into an empty destination. Export includes private maps and browser-origin policy but excludes sign-in sessions, project keys, outbox and temporary state. Run setup if the destination has no owner and create new keys after restoring. Browser restore is available from `/setup` before the first project and Settings thereafter. For CLI import of a browser download, first run `chmod 600 /path/to/spool-private-archive.jsonl`; see [the transfer procedure](OPERATIONS.md#data-movement-and-retention). Reset removes only its displayed local inventory and preserves source, exports and deployment records.
 
 ## Upgrade an existing installation
 
-Back up first: export a private archive (Settings → **Download private archive**, or stop dev and run `rer export --output exports/spool.rer`). Keep the original checkout, database and private settings.
+Back up first: export a private archive (Settings → **Download private archive**, or stop dev and run `~/.local/bin/rer export --output exports/spool.rer`). Keep the original checkout, database and private settings.
 
-For the latest tagged release, run `git fetch --tags && git checkout v0.7.11`, then `rer dev`. To keep following `main`, run `git pull --ff-only` and then `rer dev`. Hosted installations update with `rer deploy` from the original deploying checkout, retaining its private settings, generated secrets and deployment receipt; follow [the hosting update procedure](docs/HOSTED.md#update-to-a-newer-spool).
+For the latest tagged release, run `git fetch --tags && git checkout v0.7.11`, then `~/.local/bin/rer dev`. To keep following `main`, run `git pull --ff-only` and then `~/.local/bin/rer dev`. Hosted installations update with `~/.local/bin/rer deploy` from the original deploying checkout, retaining its private settings, generated secrets and deployment receipt; follow [the hosting update procedure](docs/HOSTED.md#update-to-a-newer-spool).
 
 Those commands apply any migrations missing from the installed version. This `main` checkout includes migrations through `0099`; a tag applies the migrations shipped with that tag. Existing projects, evidence, triage states, grouping rules, inbound filters, alert rules and project keys are preserved. No reset or restore is needed for an upgrade. Older native private archives can also restore into a fresh, empty current installation. See the [release record](RELEASE.json) and [changelog](CHANGELOG.md).

 ## Run it on your Cloudflare account
 
-Follow [the hosting guide](docs/HOSTED.md) to configure your account and email sender. Stop local dev with `rer dev --stop`, then run `rer deploy`. Open `/sign-in` on the printed hosted address and request an email link. If you cannot receive mail, `rer signin --env-file .rer/deploy/production.env --environment production` prints a private, one-use owner link using the hosting guide's private settings file, the same Cloudflare credentials and original deploying checkout; it expires within 15 minutes.
+Follow [the hosting guide](docs/HOSTED.md) to configure your account and email sender. Stop local dev with `~/.local/bin/rer dev --stop`, then run `~/.local/bin/rer deploy`. Open `/sign-in` on the printed hosted address and request an email link. If you cannot receive mail, `~/.local/bin/rer signin --env-file .rer/deploy/production.env --environment production` prints a private, one-use owner link using the hosting guide's private settings file, the same Cloudflare credentials and original deploying checkout; it expires within 15 minutes.
 
-To remove it, export anything you need and run `rer deploy --remove --yes` from the original deploying checkout, retaining its private deployment record and using the same account credentials. The default environment is `production`; add `--environment <name>` for another environment. Removal deletes the Worker and its database. The hosting guide also covers updates and restoring archives. `rer deploy --dry-run` builds and validates the package locally without deploying or contacting Cloudflare. It prints the plan and names the inputs a real deploy still needs. A successful dry run exits 0 even when those inputs are missing; it does not establish that a real deploy is ready.
